query: What out-of-sample temporal, sectoral calibration, adversarial checks, and update rules should be pre-specified to detect NLP concept drift and combine BERT/dictionary models into m^(s)?

response.query: What out-of-sample temporal, sectoral calibration, adversarial checks, and update rules should be pre-specified to detect NLP concept drift and combine BERT/dictionary models into m^(s)?
response.answer: To detect NLP concept drift, use out-of-sample temporal checks, sectoral calibration, adversarial validation, and predefined update rules. Combine BERT and dictionary models using ensemble methods. Ensure pre-specification of all detection and combination protocols.

results.title: Using large language models for semantic interoperability
results.content: ## ICT Express. Volume 11, Issue 4, August 2025, Pages 819-837. # Using large language models for semantic interoperability: A systematic literature review. Author links open overlay panel, , , , , ,. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.icte.2025.06.011Get rights and content. Under a Creative Commons license. Semantic Interoperability (SI) enables cross-domain data integration by allowing diverse systems to share and process information effectively. While existing reviews focus on general AI-driven interoperability, this systematic literature review (SLR) is the first to exclusively analyze the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) with SI. This SLR uniquely evaluates LLMs' role in schema alignment, knowledge integration, and security risks. It also introduces a novel taxonomy and identifies challenges like bias propagation and computational costs, providing a new research framework for adversarial robustness, ethical AI, and real-world SI optimization.
